blocker.summary: r435 found a reproducible entry-thread SIGSEGV that contradicts r431/r432's 'chain closed' claim for a full-length run. r436 root-caused it precisely via live gdb capture (3 successive breakpoints on one launch, same methodology as r412/r420-r424/r426): sub_821D6C20 does a vtable dispatch (PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC) through a global object pointer at guest address 0x82935D98 that is NULL at call time -- measured at every link of the chain: object_ptr(r3)=0x0, vtable_ptr(r11=*r3)=0x0, ctr_candidate(the function pointer that would be called)=0x0. Codegen verified faithful: the 6 x86 instructions at the crash site match ppc_recomp.23.cpp:20296 one-for-one, so this is NOT a codegen bug -- it's a genuine null-pointer dispatch through an object that was never constructed. This site was never reached before this session's cycle chain: r346 (much earlier in the campaign, artifacts/retail-us-native-r346-d6c20-dispatch-survey/) directly measured zero calls to sub_821D6C20 over 90 seconds, because the entry thread used to stall earlier (in the allocator, before r413-r415's fix). This crash is therefore a pre-existing defect first exposed by this session's own allocator/IRQL/presentation fixes unblocking deeper boot progress -- not a regression from any single recent commit. Not fixed this cycle: the object pointer being null could stem from a missing host stub for whatever subsystem constructs this object, or from an antecedent fix in this chain (r413/r422/r430) altering execution order past that construction step -- neither hypothesis is yet distinguished, and CLAUDE.md's discipline against a plausible-but-uncontrolled fix applies directly here. Named for r437: trace what should write guest address 0x82935D98 (static XEX data or a dynamic host-stub write) before attempting any fix to sub_821D6C20 itself. No source touched this cycle (live investigation only); gates/ctest unaffected from r435's state. The wider native/ backlog commit decision (r433) remains open, unrelated.
